To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the doses of heart medications in clinical practice differ from the target doses recommended by guidelines.
there are many challenges to the appropriate dosing of heart failure therapies.

(1) the target doses of most heart failure medications were not achieved in clinical trials and are not achieved in clinical practice, and (2) the target doses are not the same for all patients, and the target dose for one medication may not be achievable when using another medication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.

the dosing of medications in the context of the multiple drug classes used to treat heart failure with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and how to achieve target doses in clinical practice.

the following issues: 1) how to optimize dosing of multiple heart failure therapies in the setting of multiple drug classes, overlapping side effects, and multiple factors that may impede achieving the target dose, and 2) how to sequence these therapies to achieve guideline-directed dosing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
clinicians should aim for maximally tolerated doses, but that the optimal dose of any drug is the one that is tolerated and provides clinical benefit to each patient.
the target doses of heart failure therapies are often not achieved in clinical practice, and clinicians should be aware of this and consider the potential consequences.
the target dose of each medication is the best dose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have to be careful in the way we dose these medications and that there is a lot more to be done to understand how to best dose medications in the context of multiple other medications and in the context of the patient.
there are opportunities to achieve target dosing of multiple drugs, but that this requires close monitoring of side effects and dose adjustments to achieve target dosages.

there is a need for a better understanding of how to optimise dosing of multiple agents in the context of heart failure with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and that there are many opportunities to optimise dosages of these agents in clinical practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current evidence does not provide clear guidance on the best approach to dosing these agents in the context of the other agents being used.
there are many options for heart failure patients and clinicians should be aware of the evidence for each drug class, and use the best available evidence to guide therapy.
clinicians should aim for the target doses of the various drug classes, and should be aware of the variability of dosing in clinical practice.
